editorial:
Blind Husbands is Erich von Stroheim's 1919 directorial debut for Universal Film Manufacturing Company, adapted from his own scenario 'The Pinnacle.' Von Stroheim plays a predatory Austrian military officer who systematically pursues an American surgeon's neglected wife during an alpine vacation â€” a voyeuristic premise he wrote, directed, and starred in on a $42,000 budget. Universal retitled it for the December 7, 1919 release, and the film earned back its cost many times over, establishing von Stroheim as a major Hollywood voice. The original negative was later shortened by Universal and then destroyed in the 1940s; for decades, only an abbreviated 1924 re-release print at MoMA circulated in the United States.

The visual print is public domain â€” published in the US in 1919, the maximum 56-year copyright term expired no later than 1975 â€” but the significant rights trap is the 2021 Austrian Film Museum 4K restoration, which premiered at Vienna's Konzerthaus on October 3, 2021. That version contains new protected creative work: digitally reconstructed tinting and toning from production documents, recreated intertitles, 41 reintegrated shots, and a freshly commissioned score by Andreas Eduardo Frank. Creators must source from the pre-restoration Internet Archive copies (identifiers BlindHusbands1919 or blind-husbands-1919, both uploaded 2016) and supply their own music; any copy traceable to the AFM restoration requires clearing the score and the restoration's creative additions.
faq: Can I use Blind Husbands footage in my film, video essay, or commercial project?

Yes â€” the visual print is public domain in the United States, published in 1919. Source footage from the Internet Archive copies (identifiers BlindHusbands1919 or blind-husbands-1919), which were uploaded in 2016 before the 2021 Austrian Film Museum restoration. Do not lift footage from the AFM-restored version without separately licensing its commissioned score by Andreas Eduardo Frank and addressing the restoration's protected creative elements.
Is the 2021 Austrian Film Museum restoration of Blind Husbands free to use?

No. While the underlying film footage is public domain, the AFM restoration adds new protectable creative work â€” digital color reconstruction, recreated intertitles, and a commissioned musical composition performed and recorded for that version. Distributing or publicly screening the AFM restoration requires clearing those elements. The older, unrestored copies on the Internet Archive carry no such restrictions.
